business_problem: Boehringer Ingelheim needed to break down data silos and standardize data solutions across the enterprise while maintaining strict compliance, so researchers and business users could work faster on new medicines and other initiatives.
solution_summary: Boehringer Ingelheim built its Dataland environment on AWS to create a centralized, self-service data foundation for life-sciences work. The platform uses Amazon S3 as a data lake for both structured and unstructured information, including handwritten documents and video, while AWS Glue discovers, catalogs, prepares, and integrates data from many sources for analytics and machine-learning use cases. The resulting curated hub makes large datasets—up to multiple petabytes for external data—available across the workforce with governance guardrails and clear quality rules. By spanning two AWS Availability Zones and aligning with GxP compliance requirements, the architecture balances flexible data access with the residency and control needs of a highly regulated industry. This gives data scientists and other users a much faster starting point for insight generation and therapeutic innovation.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3
solution_components.role: Acts as Boehringer Ingelheim's centralized data lake for structured and unstructured data.

solution_components.name: AWS Glue
solution_components.role: Discovers, catalogs, prepares, and integrates datasets for analytics and ML teams.

data_flow: Enterprise and external datasets are stored in Amazon S3, discovered and prepared through AWS Glue, and then exposed through Dataland's self-service environment for analytics, visualization, and machine-learning work across the workforce.
business_outcome: Boehringer Ingelheim targeted enterprise-wide standardization in 2 years, reduced data-preparation effort so users can start within hours instead of months, exposed the platform to more than 10,000 employees, and created a compliant shared data foundation for launching new medicines faster.
